spec_match.rationale: Probes the exact detection surface: navigator.gpu.wgslLanguageFeatures.has('buffer_view'), the string confirmed in Tint's enums.cc (LanguageFeature::kBufferView -> "buffer_view") and used by the official webgpu-samples wireframe port. The page also teaches the negative contract — buffer_view is a WGSL language feature, not a GPUFeatureName — by listing the real adapter.features set alongside.

interactive.rationale: A real probe runs on load and on demand: it enumerates the full wgslLanguageFeatures set as chips, requests a real GPUAdapter, prints adapter.info, and renders one of four distinct verdicts. The probe can and does return false.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index blurb promises reading the real set, requesting a real adapter, and distinguishing no-WebGPU from WebGPU-without-buffer_view — all delivered.

edge_cases.rationale: Four honest outcomes are distinguished: no navigator.gpu, WebGPU-but-null-adapter (verified in this session by running without --enable-features=Vulkan), adapter-without-buffer_view (verified with SwiftShader), and full support. requestAdapter() throwing is also handled.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5094091886034944, the feature page, and MDN WGSLLanguageFeatures.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's buffer-view-language-feature-listed and detection-surface assertions mirror exactly what this page probes; the full suite ran in this session's browser with the honest expected matrix (detection surface pass, buffer_view absent).

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via CLI + CDP: with --enable-unsafe-webgpu --enable-features=Vulkan the page showed 4 WGSL features, buffer_view=false, SwiftShader adapter info, and the adapter-without-feature verdict; without flags it showed the null-adapter verdict; re-running via the button repopulated everything; console clean apart from Chrome's own 'WebGPU is experimental' info line. The supported verdict and the no-WebGPU branch could not be exercised in this environment (no Chrome 153 with the feature flipped).

telemetry_health.rationale: bufferview-probe-supported asserts only on the supported branch; bufferview-probe-fallback asserts separately for no-webgpu / no-adapter / feature-missing with state details, so a fallback is never reported as a pass.

design_system.rationale: Only CSS variables; the ok-verdict uses black-on-emerald (~5.1:1) after the ivory-on-emerald (~4.0:1) draft was caught and fixed; rose verdict ivory-on-rose ~5.3:1; focus-visible outlines throughout.

accessibility.rationale: Native button, aria-live=polite on both verdict and status, chip lists carry aria-label, key/value readouts use dl semantics, headings are sequential, and focus is visible. Status text summarises the probe outcome for non-visual users after each run.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360x740 DPR3 mobile: documentElement.scrollWidth 360 (no horizontal overflow) after adding code{overflow-wrap:anywhere}; full-page mobile and 1280x1600 desktop screenshots read and checked; panels reflow via auto-fit minmax grid with min-width:0. Note: plain CLI --window-size=360 screenshots hit the known headless min-width clamp, so CDP emulation was used for the authoritative check.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel layout without horizontal overflow mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use flex-wrap on control rows and grid with flexible minmax()/auto-fit tracks plus min-width:0 on children instead of fixed widths.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The four probe panels use grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(250px,1fr)) with min-width:0 children; the control row is flex with wrap; verified zero horizontal overflow at 360px via CDP.

guidanceConsulted.query: announce async operation result status live region
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use landmarks, sequential headings, native controls, and polite live regions for asynchronous state changes.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Verdict and status are aria-live=polite output/div elements updated after the async probe completes; chips lists are real ul/li with aria-label.

openQuestions.title: Supported-path verdict untested in a real browser
openQuestions.detail: No available browser in this environment lists buffer_view (Chromium 141 + SwiftShader tops out at 4 shipped WGSL features), so the green full-support verdict has only been code-reviewed, not observed. Re-verify on Chrome 153+/Canary with chrome://flags/#enable-unsafe-webgpu once available.

summary: The probe reads the exact wgslLanguageFeatures surface the feature ships on, renders the real returned set, and cleanly separates the four failure/success states; the two reachable fallback states were both observed in this session's headless Chromium 141 (SwiftShader adapter present vs no adapter), with clean console and no mobile overflow. The one real gap is that the supported branch cannot be observed until a build with buffer_view flipped exists.
